title: Failed Magnate Backs Call for Deportation of Fellow Mexicans – Soberanía 116
author: Mexico Solidarity
content:
In episode 116 of Soberanía, hosts José Luis Granados Ceja and Kurt Hackbarth
open with Claudia Sheinbaum's last-minute trip to New York for the World Cup
final — and the overwhelming reception she received from the Mexican migrant
community. The hosts contrast this with the reaction of oligarch Ricardo
Salinas Pliego, who responded to video of the welcoming crowd by retweeting a
tweet with the text **" ICE do your thing,"** effectively calling for the
agency to target his own compatriots.

Next, they analyze the life sentence handed down to Ismael "El Mayo" Zambada —
and the death of the opposition's fever dream that he would "sing" and
implicate AMLO, Sheinbaum, or Morena, dashing the hopes of those who spent
months insinuating otherwise, including former ambassador Ken Salazar, who
peddled the rumor for the grubby purpose of increasing book sales.

The episode then covers the dismantling of the largest fuel-smuggling network
in the country, linked to former Baja California governor Ernesto Ruffo Appel,
who allegedly defrauded the treasury of over 4 billion pesos. The hosts note
the irony of the right-wing opposition immediately crying "political prisoner"
while simultaneously launching a new political party whose first major cause
is defending an accused gasoline smuggler. The hosts also highlight a scoop
from colleague Jesús García: weapons linked to the U.S. State Department have
been seized from criminal groups in Tamaulipas, adding yet another chapter to
the long history of U.S. arms ending up in cartel hands.

Losers and Haters takes aim at the right-wing echo chamber — from Kenya López
Rabadán calling Ruffo a political prisoner to columnist Sergio Sarmiento
defending him with the flimsiest of pretexts.
